question.text: Shivalik Sustainable Fund (Cat I-Infrastructure) is being set up as a trust. The sponsor asks whether the trustee needs to be a 'SEBI-Registered Trustee' (as required for Mutual Funds under SEBI (MF) Regulations, 1996). What is the correct position under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: Yes, only a SEBI-Registered Trustee under SEBI (Trustee) Regulations can be appointed
The trustee must be a scheduled commercial bank with asset base > INR 1000 crore
There is NO requirement to appoint a SEBI-Registered Trustee; however, SEBI has laid down a Code of Conduct for trustees and reviews the appointment at the time of AIF registration
The trustee must be registered with IBBI

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter, 'there is no requirement for appointment of a Registered SEBI Trustee under SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012'. The regulations don't prescribe qualification/certification/legal form for AIF trustees, but DO specify a Code of Conduct. SEBI reviews the appointment at registration, and subsequent changes need SEBI approval. The Trap: The SEBI-Registered Trustee option wrongly imports the Mutual Fund regime. The bank-only option invents a rule. The IBBI option confuses with Insolvency valuation registration. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers this contrast. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) may compare AIF trustee regime vs MF trustee regime. MF track (V-A/V-B) has the SEBI-Registered Trustee mandate — don't import to AIF. Manager's Pro-Tip: Though not mandatory, most serious Cat I/II funds do appoint an established independent trustee company (Axis Trustee, IDBI Trusteeship, Vistra) — LPs expect it. Trustee fees typically INR 5-15 lakh/year; negotiate scope-of-work carefully to avoid scope creep.
